entities.span: The tool is undecided and belongs to feature 25's design pass. The entry already names `defuddle`, but nothing browser related is installed yet, no Playwright, Puppeteer, defuddle or Browserbase. Playwright is this repo's recorded end to end choice and is supported on Vercel Functions; a hosted service such as Browserbase is a separate vendor decision with its own terms and cost.
The gate itself is unchanged and is not a tool question: fetching the destination page is a third party terms and robots question that Adzuna's own terms don't resolve either way.

**First hard measurement, 2026-09-15.** A real refresh scored 8 real Adzuna listings against two candidate profiles, and **6 of the 8 own role rows came back with zero matched skills at all**, on postings whose titles match the candidate's own first desired title. The cause is the 500 character excerpt Adzuna returns, which usually carries company boilerplate rather than requirements. That result fired spec 0021's own pre-registered stopping rule, which concluded the snippet is the cause and froze the two demo queries rather than re-tuning them, so the measurement closes a question instead of opening one.
rejected_spans: Until this date both this item and the JobsPipe alternative below were argued from the shape of the data rather than from a number.
This is the information gap both items are about, now measured on real postings and a real scorer.

entities.label: First hard measurement, 2026-09-15

entities.span: **A v2 consideration, not v1 or v1.5: JobsPipe (https://jobspipe.dev) as an alternative to the approach above, not an addition to it.** It would remove the need for a second request and any HTML parsing, Verified 2026-09-08 against their OpenAPI spec (jobspipe.dev/openapi.json) and terms page, the `Job` schema's `description` field reads "Full text of the posting as published by the source", against Adzuna's 500 character excerpt; it also returns `seniority`, `work_arrangement` (remote/hybrid/onsite), `status` (active/closed), `keyword_slugs`, `min/max_annual_salary_usd`, and `discovered_at` for incremental polling; credits are 1 per job returned, `blur_company_data=true` returns rows for zero credits, the free tier is 1,000 jobs a month with `limit` capped at 25 (about 50 searches a month at 20 listings each, against the current cap of roughly 108), and the first paid tier is $49 a month for 25,000; their terms state no attribution requirement, which would make spec 0013's AC-6 and AC-7 apparatus (the attribution component, the logo geometry, the mandated link targets) deletable rather than portable; their terms do **not** address caching or storage, a gap rather than a permission, and this app stores listing fields on `application` rows, so that has to be resolved with the vendor in writing before anyone relies on it. Two other places already point at this same decision, so treat it as one rather than three: `docs/feature-14-v2-architecture.md`'s extract-then-score pipeline names full posting text as its own unmet precondition and is not referenced anywhere else in this scope; and spec 0016's Consequences already names the switching cost, that feature 15's sixteen ground truth pairs stop matching what the model sees the moment full postings arrive and need a deliberate re-authoring pass.
rejected_spans: since the full text arrives in the search response itself
recorded so a later session need not re-fetch:
entities.label: A v2 consideration, not v1 or v1.5: JobsPipe (https://jobspipe.dev) as an alternative to the approach above, not an addition to it.

entities.span: **An aggregate scoring deadline**: a cutoff shorter than the per call 30 second timeout, after which any listing still pending in a fit-scoring batch renders as a failure rather than waiting out its own call. Not built in feature 14: trades completeness for responsiveness with no acceptance criterion requiring it, and an abandoned call still spends its `usage_cap` unit either way. Revisit if real usage shows the full worst case wait happens often enough to matter.
entities.label: An aggregate scoring deadline
